headline: Roseland and Morgan Park anchor a ward strong on school funding, thin on nightlife.
summary:
Ward 21 covers Washington Heights, West Pullman, Morgan Park, and Roseland on Chicago's Far South Side. It comes in 34th citywide, with a combined score of 37.04. A caveat attaches to most of what gets measured here, 164 of the 181 rankings this ward has on record.

The strongest numbers cluster around schools and streets. Per-pupil school spending ranks 2nd citywide, and just over 97 percent of the ward's aldermanic menu money went toward resurfacing streets, a top-3 share in Chicago. The weak spots sit on the retail and nightlife side. Ward 21 has the highest share of chain restaurants in the city, no bars rated 4.5 stars or better with at least 50 reviews, and almost no restaurants licensed to serve liquor. That combination points to a residential ward where schools and street paving are the visible public investment, not a built-out commercial strip.
reading_the_rankings: Three of Ward 21's six best rankings track religious attendance, and all three come from one demographic model rather than a survey conducted here. Wards with a population mix like this one turn up nearly identical numbers by construction, and the estimate carries a low confidence rating from its source, so the weekly-attendance and strongly-religious figures describe a modeled pattern, not a count of who showed up on a given Sunday. The alley-repair and spending-diversity rankings near the bottom are the flip side of that street-paving strength. With 97 percent of menu money going to streets, little was left for alleys or anything else, which is why both land in the mid-40s citywide. The liquor-license ranking, 49th in the city, looks worse than the gap behind it. Twelve wards are effectively tied with Ward 21 here, the whole group sitting inside a two-point spread.

news.headline: South Siders Still Waiting For Tree Cleanup After June Storms, But City Departments Are Overwhelmed
news.note: June storms left about 1,600 tree-related 311 requests open in Ward 21, the second-highest count of any ward, with hundreds still unresolved three weeks later.

news.headline: City program to rehab more than 30 properties on the South and West sides is back
news.note: Rebuild Chicago 2.0 is using a $20 million state grant to rehab and resell 33 vacant homes in Roseland and Englewood.
